tob-10043: Israel Abrahams, a noted Jewish scholar, gathers here his essays and translations on Jewish literature and history. The title essay presents ‘The Book of Delight,’ a medieval Hebrew work of wit and wisdom, in English for the first time for many readers. The remaining papers touch on Jewish life, letters, and learning across the centuries, opening a little-known corner of world literature.
tob-13643: Presented as the distilled wisdom of Hermes Trismegistus, the thrice-great sage of Egypt, The Kybalion lays out seven universal laws — including the law of attraction’s ancestor, the principle of vibration. The Three Initiates wrote it for the early twentieth-century seeker, packaging ancient-seeming doctrine in crisp modern prose. It endures as a gateway text of the occult revival.
tob-4043: Poet and playwright Friedrich Schiller turned thinker in these essays on beauty, art, and human freedom. He holds that the play of beauty can make us whole, joining our feeling side to our reasoning side. Set down in the 1790s, these essays steered German views of art and schooling for a hundred years.
tob-4243: Lady Charlotte Guest’s Mabinogion bears the Welsh wonder-tales into English — Pwyll’s otherworld ride, Bran’s doomed sailing, the spells of Math and Gwydion. Her 1849 rendering, bettered in 1877, was a milestone of Celtic learning. The tales shine with a strangeness no later hand has dulled.
tob-10543: Macauliffe’s Religion of the Sikhs is the classic English account of Sikhism — the lives of the ten Gurus and the teachings of the Granth Sahib. His six-volume work introduced the faith to the Western world. The book remains the foundational English Sikh history.
tob-13143: Swami Vivekananda’s Karma Yoga teaches the path of selfless work — freedom through action without clinging to results. His Chicago lectures made the Gita’s teaching practical for modern readers. Work becomes worship when the ego steps aside. The book remains a beloved introduction to yoga’s active path.
tob-14243: The Rising-Treatise — Nag Hammadi’s first book, fourth tract — is the Gnostic letter on rising from the dead, in Barnstone and Peel’s Englishing. Its love-teaching mingles Paul and Gnosis. The text is a jewel of the Nag Hammadi hoard.
cia-0000107443: Dated January 1947, this report covers communists and the Palestine question, including missions to Russia and a new head of the Armenian church. It is a collage of early Cold War fragments from a world being remade — the Palestine mandate ending, churches reorganizing, communists maneuvering. The young CIA was learning to watch everything at once.
cia-0000112343: An October 1991 report on strip mining polluting Dalnegorsk in Russia's Maritime Kray — the archive's spelling of Krai. Open-pit mining was poisoning the land around this Far Eastern town. Filed as the Soviet Union dissolved, the entry shows environmental damage surfacing as a subject the old regime could no longer hide.
cia-0000119743: The situation in Hungary as of 4:00 PM Washington time on October 30, 1956 — filed in the capital's own time zone for officials racing the clock. Soviet troops seemed to be leaving; Hungarian independence seemed possible. The timestamped hope in this report makes what followed even harder to read.
cia-0000126943: An estimated April 1986 terrorism review on the attack against the American chancery in La Paz, Bolivia. Striking the U.S. embassy's offices was a direct challenge to American presence. The document records the incident and its meaning: Bolivia's radicals aiming at the eagle.
cia-0000132143: A European brief for August 18, 1988 — leading, like its Middle East sibling, with the crash that killed Pakistan's president and the U.S. ambassador. The same catastrophe echoed across regional briefs. The document shows one event rippling through every corner of the intelligence world.
cia-0000132643: A May 1960 report: Venezuelan-Cuban relations deteriorating. The friendship was failing — Caracas moving toward the break. The document is the deterioration: the neighbors, estranged.
cia-0000132743: A 1960 report on Cuba and Central America. The island's shadow fell across the isthmus. The document is the region, linked: the revolution's reach, mapped.
cia-0000135943: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN reporting the identification of a contact. A face to a name. The document is the identification: the contact, known.
cia-0000136243: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN stating opposition to bomb drop instructions. Someone objected to the bombing orders. The document is the dissent: the instructions, opposed.
cia-0000136343: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CADICK transmitting a message from Guatemala on meetings with D-someone — the truncated title cuts off the name. The relayed report. The entry is the transmission: the meetings, described.
cia-0000139043: An untitled 1954 document on Gerhart Eisler. The operative, revisited. The document is the file: the man, noted.
un-ga-res-43: UN General Assembly Resolution 43, adopted in 1946. The postwar world was being rebuilt in resolutions — each one a small brick in the new order. The catalog records the number and year; the resolution's text records the will of the members.
un-ga-res-a-69-43: Resolution A/69/43, cataloged with the year 1996 — the session number and year disagree. The entry preserves the designation and questions the date.
un-sc-res-143: Security Council Resolution 143, adopted in July 1960 — the Congo resolution, calling on Belgium to withdraw its troops from the newly independent republic. Days after independence, the Council confronted the Congo crisis head-on. The resolution is the demand: the troops, out.
un-sc-res-243: Security Council Resolution 243, adopted in 1967. The deliberations continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1843: Security Council Resolution 1843, adopted in 2008 — aligned. The Council deciding. The designation and year are preserved; the act belongs to the text.
cia-0000135643: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000135643. The brigade's Spanish voice, another volume. The document is the volume: the words, theirs.
cia-0000135743: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135743. The Bay of Pigs force, on paper in Spanish. The entry is the paper: the force, documented.
cia-0000136643: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136643, the archive's date uncertain. The approximately dated documents. The document is the approximation: the year, circa.
plos-pone-0000043: A 2006 PLOS ONE paper asking: is adipose tissue a place for Mycobacterium tuberculosis persistence? Does TB hide in body fat? The question reframes where the bacterium lurks. The paper is the question: the fat, suspected.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d43: President Roosevelt to Marshal Stalin, October 14, 1943 — Document 43. A second letter the same day. The message is the second: the day, doubled.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d143: President Roosevelt to Prime Minister Churchill, November 19, 1943 — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 143. Washington answered the same day. The message is the quickness: the reply, immediate.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d243: The Secretary of State to the President, November 21, 1943 — Document 243. The department briefed the White House. The memo is the briefing: the secretary, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d343: The final text of the communiqué — the truncated title cuts off the date — Document 343. The announcement, finished. The text is the final: the words, agreed.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d443: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 5, 1943 — Document 443. The Allied planners, minuted. The minutes are the planners': the chiefs, combined.
arxiv-2605-08843: Simulating physics on a computer means chopping continuous reality into discrete chunks, and the training objective has to respect that chopping. Yuan Mei, Xingyu Song, Xiaowen Song, and Naoya Takeishi reframe the training measures used for discretized physical simulations. The 2026 paper is about making machine-learned simulators honest about their own discretization.
arxiv-2605-09043: Words drift in emotional meaning — what freedom feels like shifts over time — and sometimes the drift snaps like a phase transition. Napassorn Litchiowong studies affective meaning divergence, hunting the hidden drift that precedes the break. The 2026 paper is computational linguistics on how the feelings attached to words change.
arxiv-2605-09343: Vision-language-action models fumble scenes they do not understand structurally. Zeyu Li and Lei Li give them scene knowledge graph priors — SKG-VLA — for structured semantics and multimodal reasoning for decision making. The 2026 paper grounds robot perception in explicit scene knowledge.
arxiv-2605-09243: Brain recordings — fMRI, EEG — are expensive to collect, so their value for machine learning needs quantifying. Lane Lewis and Zhixin Wang ask how much brain data is actually worth for ML. The 2026 paper is a cost-benefit analysis for neuro-AI.
arxiv-2605-09543: Modeling starlight without assuming local thermodynamic equilibrium — non-LTE — is accurate and agonizingly slow in 3D. A. Vicente Arévalo, A. Asensio Ramos, and C. J. Díaz Baso accelerate the synthesis with graph neural networks. The 2026 paper is solar physics at machine speed.
arxiv-2605-10043: Personalizing LLMs from binary feedback — thumbs up, thumbs down — with preference-corrected optimization. Xilai Ma, Liye Zhao, Weijun Yao, and colleagues build the framework. The 2026 paper is personalization from the simplest possible signal. It learns rich preferences from binary choices.
plos-pone-0003443: Microbiologists tested whether bacterial RNA survives in bottled water in this 2008 study. Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli were stored long-term in mineral water while the team tracked RNA stability, a marker of whether the cells were still viable. The work matters for water safety testing, since detecting live germs hinges on knowing what RNA persists.
plos-pone-0003543: Neuroscientists found swollen brain cells venting chemicals two ways in this 2008 rat study. When brain tissue swells, cells release excitatory amino acids and taurine through distinct channels depending on the osmotic trigger. Distinguishing the two release modes clarifies how the brain handles the dangerous swelling of stroke and injury.
plos-pone-0003643: In 2008, a team watched a DNA repair protein reshape how DNA is packed. Rad51, the key player in swapping matching DNA strands, formed long chains on single strands, and that chaining loosened the packed DNA around it. The result ties repair work to a change in how DNA is stored.
plos-pone-0003743: In 2008, Lenselink, Melchers, and Quint mapped HPV before the vaccine era. Among Dutch women aged 18 to 29, they linked sexual behavior patterns to HPV infection rates. The pre-vaccine baseline shows what the virus was doing on its own, before shots changed the picture.
plos-pone-0003843: A 2008 statistics paper tackled missing patients in HIV programs. Yiannoutsos, An, and Frangakis developed sampling-based methods to estimate death rates among patients lost to follow-up. The approach corrects the rosy bias of counting only those who stay in care.
plos-pone-0003943: In 2008, Beyrouthy, Alexander, and Baldwin hunted genes active in the cell cycle's first phase. They identified G1-regulated genes in normally dividing human cells. The catalog gives cell-cycle researchers markers that work without artificial synchronization.
plos-pone-0004043: In 2008, Ohlendorf, Sprenger, and Speck mapped motion vision around the center. Optic flow stimuli in and near the visual field center activated motion-sensitive regions. One-sided motion lit the opposite brain side while quieting the same side. The group brain-scan study charts how central vision handles self-movement.
plos-pone-0004143: In 2009, Gioiosa, Chiarotti, and Alleva found company changing pain. A mouse's pain response shifted with social context and rank sharply. Dyads of mice felt pain differently in pairs than alone. The neat result ties pain to social life, even in mice.
plos-pone-0004243: In 2009, Bjorklund, Svedlund, and Olsson found a shortened receptor feeding human breast cancer. The internally truncated LRP5 receptor marked a clear therapeutic target. The stubby receptor drove WNT signaling in tumors. Blocking it could starve breast cancers of growth signals.
plos-pone-0004343: In 2009, Beduneau, Ma, and Grotepas turned immune cells into drug couriers. Monocyte-macrophage uptake of superparamagnetic iron-oxide nanoparticles was boosted. The loaded cells carried cargo to tissues. The method merges diagnostics and delivery. The approach exploits cells that infections already target.
plos-pone-0358643: Artificial intelligence systems often cannot explain their choices, which makes people reluctant to trust them. This paper presents a framework that pairs predictions with plain-language explanations and what-if alternatives, so a decision-maker can see how changing the inputs would change the outcome. The authors test the approach as a decision-support tool, aiming for AI that advises people instead of simply handing down answers.
plos-pone-0358043: Some bladder cancers shrug off immunotherapy, and this paper found a possible reason why. The authors describe a recurring pattern — fibroblasts, TGF-beta signals, and blood-vessel barriers — that keeps immune cells out of the tumor, driving resistance to checkpoint drugs. Naming this barrier points drug developers toward new targets for patients immunotherapy fails.
plos-pone-0358543: People with HIV faced brutal COVID risks — until vaccines arrived. This population-based Florida study compared COVID-19 mortality among people with HIV before and after vaccine introduction. The before-and-after picture quantifies exactly how much vaccination changed survival for this vulnerable group.
plos-pone-0339543: Inflammatory breast cancer is rare and aggressive — new drug combinations are urgently needed. This paper went from in silico prediction to experimental validation, identifying drugs and synergistic combinations that inhibit the cancer’s growth. The pipeline turns pure computation into genuine candidates for the clinic.
plos-pone-0358243: After a stopped heart is restarted, families ask the hardest question: will they wake up? This research tested bedside ultrasound to quickly evaluate neurological prognosis in patients with return of spontaneous circulation. The quick scan could give doctors an early, honest answer when every hour of uncertainty hurts.
plos-pone-0347443: Lupus patients’ immune systems are already on edge — and donor blood can tip them over. This multi-cohort analysis linked type I interferon signature strength to alloimmunization-associated gene programs in systemic lupus erythematosus. The signature may predict which patients will react badly to transfusions before the blood is given.
plos-pone-0355343: Thyroid cancer imaging just got a better tracer. This paper showed 68Ga-FAPI-04 PET/CT achieves high diagnostic efficacy in both Tg-positive and Tg-negative differentiated thyroid cancer. The tracer finds tumors that older imaging misses — including the tricky Tg-negative cases.
plos-pone-0332243: Did state-level or county-level mask mandates damage the economy differently during COVID-19? This paper measured the impact of each mandate level on economic activity across the pandemic. The comparison gives future policymakers evidence — not ideology — about how to calibrate public health orders.
plos-pone-0357443: Wild thyme gathered in Palestine carries chemistry worth bottling. This paper analyzed the essential oil composition and biological activities of Coridothymus capitatus collected from two Palestinian locations. The oils showed genuine promise — antimicrobial, antioxidant, and distinctly local.
plos-pone-0357043: Operative vaginal delivery — forceps or vacuum — carries real neonatal risks. This study at the University of Gondar Comprehensive Specialized Hospital examined adverse neonatal outcomes and their associated factors. The findings help obstetric teams in similar settings deliver safer care.
plos-pone-0356143: Influence flows through trust — and trust shifts over time. This paper modeled and optimized trust-mediated influence in temporal heterogeneous networks. The mathematics maps how persuasion actually propagates through changing social structures.
plos-pone-0355543: Young children can’t articulate their own questions — but they learn constantly in museums. This paper studied learning and visitor dynamics among the very young in a constructivist museum environment. The findings help museums design for visitors too young to ask their own questions.
plos-pone-0355943: Wind turbines inject messy power into grids — and quality matters. This paper enhanced power quality in wind energy applications through E2PLL-based DSTATCOM control. The advanced control scheme smooths the electrical output, making wind power a better grid citizen.
plos-pone-0350743: Bumble bee wings wear down with age and foraging — and fractal geometry can measure it. This paper quantified wing wear using fractal analysis. The elegant method turns ragged wing edges into precise numbers, giving ecologists a new tool for aging wild bees and assessing colony stress.
plos-pone-0352643: Rural Kenya’s mental health treatment gap is vast — but primary care might close it. This stepped-wedge trial tested strategies for reducing the diagnostic and treatment gap for priority mental, neurological, and substance use disorders in rural primary care. The results offer a scalable model for places with almost no specialists.
plos-pone-0355043: Flying squirrels glide, tree squirrels leap — and their mitochondrial genomes record the evolutionary split. This paper drew insights into adaptive evolution across locomotor modes and squirrel phylogeny from mitogenomes of flying and tree squirrels. The genetic analysis reveals how the demands of gliding versus climbing sculpted these rodents’ DNA over millions of years.
plos-pone-0342143: Social media platforms don’t just host polarization — their mechanisms manufacture it. This paper examined platform mechanisms and the dynamics of emotional polarization in the digital public. The analysis reveals how design choices — not just human nature — drive societies apart, pointing to fixes in the machinery itself.
plos-pone-0345143: Ant guest social parasites infiltrate colonies that should tear them apart — using venom as a peace signal. This paper showed these parasites avoid conflict with social hosts through venom signaling. The chemical diplomacy reveals an evolutionary arms race resolved not by force but by pharmacology.
plos-pone-0354343: Teenagers who do muscle-strengthening exercise differ from those who don’t — in discoverable ways. This machine learning analysis identified the correlates of muscle strengthening exercise in adolescents. The ML-derived profiles help public health target the teens most likely to skip strength training — and understand why.
plos-pone-0355843: Neonatal meningitis kills quickly in settings with limited resources. This Harar, Ethiopia cross-sectional study examined treatment outcomes and associated factors among neonates admitted to public hospitals. The findings identify what separates survival from death — guiding care where every resource counts.
plos-pone-0355743: Pelleting feed and adding enzymes can unlock nutrition from tough ingredients. This precision-fed study examined pelleting and beta-mannanase effects on nutrient digestibility and metabolizable energy of DDGS, copra meal, palm kernel meal, and jatropha meal. The findings help feed formulators squeeze more nutrition from cheaper ingredients.
plos-pone-0342443: Visually impaired children’s quality of life hinges on functional vision — what they can actually do with their sight. This paper showed functional vision promotes quality of life and socio-emotional functioning in these children and adolescents. The findings argue for rehabilitation focused on usable vision, not just acuity charts.
europmc-pmc2825543: Cells under stress must choose between surviving and dying, and this 2010 review maps the decision. The authors survey cellular stress responses, covering the pathways that lead to either recovery or programmed death. Their overview connects many kinds of stress to a common logic. The review is a useful entry point to a central question in cell biology.
europmc-pmc2831043: Screening for anxiety in Spanish requires a properly adapted tool. This 2010 paper describes the cultural adaptation of the GAD-7 scale into Spanish. The authors validate it as a screening instrument for generalized anxiety disorder. The adapted scale gave Spanish-speaking clinics a reliable, brief anxiety measure.
europmc-pmc2860243: The protein Oct4 keeps stem cells young, but it does not work alone. This 2010 paper maps an Oct4-centered protein interaction network in embryonic stem cells. The authors chart its many partners. Their web shows pluripotency is a team effort.
europmc-pmc2873343: Africa lacks enough doctors for its HIV burden, so nurses and aides fill the gap. This 2010 review assesses task-shifting for HIV treatment and care in Africa. The authors find the shift works when done right. Their review backed a practical fix to a staffing crisis.
europmc-pmc2944843: Tumors feel their surroundings, and stiffness shapes them. This 2010 paper shows matrix rigidity steers cancer cell growth and cell form. The authors prove the world around a tumor sculpts it. Their finding matters for lab-grown tumor models and future therapy.
europmc-pmc3032643: IBD guts carry jumbled germs. This 2011 paper compares germ mixes in sore versus calm patches of bowel. The authors map where the imbalance strikes. Their work points to targeted therapies. Sore patches teem with the wrong crowd. Calm patches keep a healthier roster.
europmc-pmc3069743: Crystal data wrangling got an intro. This 2011 primer walks through sorting crystal data: symmetry, scaling, and stats. The author's guide taught crystallographers the ropes. The steps turn spots into structures. Every crystallographer learns these steps first. Bad scaling ruins good crystals, it warns.
europmc-pmc3081743: Blind patients read with chip implants. This 2011 trial shows under-retina chips letting blind patients read letters and build words. The authors restore partial sight. Their work pioneered the bionic eye. Patients read their own names again. The implants need no external camera.
europmc-pmc6570943: DNA wraps around histone spools, and swapping in the variant H2A.Z changes which genes can be read. This review tracks the histone variant's jobs: flipping genes on and off, helping repair DNA, and organizing chromosome centers. When H2A.Z goes rogue it aids cancer - making it both a basic-science star and a therapeutic suspect.
europmc-pmc6582343: Animal cells carry a tiny second genome in their mitochondria - handy for tracing evolution, but a chore to piece together from raw sequencing data. MitoZ is a one-stop toolkit that assembles these mini-genomes, labels their genes, and draws clear pictures. Researchers studying animal family trees get from raw reads to results with far less fuss.
europmc-pmc6618043: Ion mobility mass spectrometry sorts molecules by shape as well as mass - but labs report results inconsistently. This community guide standardizes what to measure and how to report it, including uncertainties for mobility and collision cross-section values. Common reporting rules let results be compared and trusted across labs.
europmc-pmc6618143: Macrophages rewire their metabolism as they switch jobs - and the metabolic fingerprint reveals which mode they are in. This review maps the metabolic signatures of macrophage responses: how energy pathways shift between fighting germs and healing tissue. Reading a cell's metabolism may soon diagnose its immune state.
europmc-pmc6631643: Pancreatic cancer's deadliness gets an assist from immune cells: macrophages mail tumor-boosting microRNA-501-3p inside exosomes. This study shows the macrophage-derived parcels drive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma forward. Blocking this cross-talk could cut a supply line the tumor depends on.
europmc-pmc6723943: Vinegar's sharp tang comes from acetate - and gut bacteria brew it too. This review explores how the short-chain fatty acid acetate influences body weight and insulin sensitivity. The smallest metabolites, it turns out, can pull outsized levers on metabolism.
europmc-pmc6742443: Textbooks draw plant mitochondrial DNA as a neat circle - but reality is messier. This study reveals the alternative reality: plant mitochondrial genomes come as a shifting mix of linear, branched, and circular forms. One ring does not rule them all - the classic map was an oversimplification.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-43: Another 2007 Government Accountability Office report on the nation's switch from analog to digital television. It argues that federal agencies needed stronger planning and risk management to keep the transition on track — particularly around public education and the converter-box coupon program. The findings warn that without tighter coordination, millions of households could lose over-the-air TV service when analog signals went dark.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-643: The Navy's repair shops could not trust their own numbers in 2007 — GAO's report says the air warfare center's books needed management action. The findings target the working-capital fog. The report's moral: a repair depot that cannot count cannot price.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-143: The Army's chemical defense units were not ready in 2007, and GAO's report says management action was needed to close the preparedness gap. The findings target the shortfalls. The report warns that the gas masks and suits had to match the threat. The readiness gap could not stand.
openalex-w7204566843: After bowel surgery, a leak where the intestine was rejoined can be deadly. This paper studies a technique that helps surgeons check blood flow during the operation: injecting a green dye that glows under special light. The authors review how this fluorescence imaging prevents leaks and guides decisions on the table. A surgical innovation where seeing better means healing better.
openalex-w7204169643: Medical students took their lessons to a quilombola community in southwest Bahia, teaching mosquito-borne disease and viral hepatitis prevention. This experience report describes the outreach project: what the students did, what the community taught them back, and how health education works outside the classroom. A first-hand account of medicine as service.
openalex-w7133357343: Chest cancer treatment is advancing fast. This review covers new drug milestones for lung malignancies: next-generation targeted pills and immune checkpoint drugs with striking survival gains. The authors surveyed both small-cell and non-small-cell disease. An oncology review of a field in rapid motion.
openalex-w7204757643: Virus-killing materials need not rely on rare earths. This paper reports iodate compounds built from common elements, tested for antiviral power and coated onto textile fibers. The authors also checked the powder forms. A materials study of everyday elements fighting germs.
pmc-13561343: This 2026 research paper compares cheaper ways to survey ocean life using eDNA — tiny traces of DNA animals leave behind in seawater. Tested at one coastal site, the team found that simpler, lower-cost water filtering and repeat sampling detect just as many species as pricier methods. That matters because it lets conservation teams monitor marine diversity with smaller budgets.
pmc-13453443: A 2026 case-based paper on the challenges of treating mpox in a patient with advanced AIDS and overlapping opportunistic infections. Managing anesthesia and procedures in someone this immunocompromised requires careful trade-offs. The paper walks through the decisions so clinicians facing similar cases have a roadmap.
pmc-13613343: This 2026 rehabilitation study found that the structural severity of lumbar spinal stenosis — narrowing of the lower spine's canal — does not predict how well patients respond to exercise-based rehab. Even patients with severe narrowing on scans improved. The finding reassures clinicians and patients that imaging severity shouldn't rule out conservative care.
pmc-13456743: In this 2026 study, patients with type 2 diabetes treated with IL-6 receptor blockers — anti-inflammatory drugs — had their cerebrospinal fluid metabolites measured to see how the drugs reach the brain's chemistry. The metabolite shifts hint at central effects of systemic inflammation control. It is a small window into the diabetes-brain connection.
pmc-13492343: This 2026 perspective traces the legacy of a Plant Physiology classic — from wrinkled seeds to plant oil accumulation networks. The retrospective shows how one paper's insights grew into a field. It is a celebration of foundational plant science.
pmc-13247843: A 2026 global cohort study of pathology and genetics across parkinsonian disorders. Comparing diseases side by side in a worldwide sample reveals shared and distinct mechanisms. The cohort is the resource.
pmc-13559643: In this 2026 cancer paper, pan-cancer and single-cell sequencing analysis illuminated the role of KIAA1467 in breast cancer. The poorly characterized gene emerged as relevant. The multi-scale analysis is the approach.
pmc-13470443: A 2026 Swedish retrospective cohort study linking mental health screening to healthcare utilization among refugees and asylum seekers. Screening changes care patterns. The findings inform refugee health policy.
pmc-13530843: This 2026 conference poster reported coronal plane alignment after pre-pubertal ACL reconstruction from the PLUTO Study Group. Growing knees need special study. The poster presents the alignment results.
pmc-13502743: In this 2026 case report, H. pylori-negative gastric MALT lymphoma achieved complete remission following eradication therapy. The unexpected response is the story. The case challenges assumptions.
pmc-13478843: A 2026 biotechnology paper exploring length and hydrophobicity requirements for optimal alpha-amylase secretion in Bacillus subtilis based on rational design. The enzyme's export was engineered. The design rules are the finding.
pmc-13461043: In this 2026 paper, plastic biodegradation potential was predicted within microbial lineages and across global ecosystems. The planet's plastic-eating capacity was mapped. The predictions guide bioprospecting.
pmc-13453943: In this 2026 imaging paper, lymphatic drainage of cerebrospinal fluid was traced using copper-64-labeled bacterial extracellular vesicles with PET (the title is truncated). The brain's drainage was visualized. The tracing is the technique.
pmc-13446143: In this 2026 Parkinson's paper, inhaled levodopa improved quality of life and non-motor symptoms associated with OFF episodes. The rescue inhaler's benefits were measured. The improvement is the evidence.
pmc-13434443: In this 2026 systematic review (the title is truncated), limited comparative evidence was found between metabolic bariatric surgery and incretin-based pharmacotherapy for weight loss in type 2 diabetes. The evidence gap was documented. The review calls for trials.
pmc-13489943: This 2026 author correction amended a paper on the sleep chart of biological ageing clocks in middle and late life. Corrections fix the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13401143: This 2026 protocol evaluated co-design and implementation of a multicomponent intervention to improve communication in aged care — a nested process evaluation (the title is truncated). The protocol is the plan. The evaluation will test the co-design.
pmc-13463543: This 2026 biomaterials paper used design-of-experiment-assisted development of biodegradable chitosan/whey protein films as advanced pro-regenerative wound dressings. The films were optimized for healing. The development is the method.
pmc-13457943: This 2026 Swedish study examined pharmacological treatment after a first myocardial infarction — long-term adherence and prognosis. The heart attack survivors' drug persistence was tracked. The adherence-prognosis link is the finding.
pmc-13574843: In this 2026 orthopedic paper, hemophilia increased risk of bleeding and thromboembolism after total shoulder arthroplasty. The clotting disorder's double risk was quantified. The increase guides perioperative care.
pmc-13509943: A 2026 review of recent advances in lipid nanoparticle-mediated respiratory and gastrointestinal mucosal delivery of nucleic acids. The mucosal mRNA delivery frontier was surveyed. The advances are the state of the field.
pmc-13448043: This 2026 narrative review covered sacral slanting in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis — definition, pathomechanism, and surgical implications. The spinal deformity's sacral aspect was reviewed. The review guides surgeons.
pmc-13447743: A 2026 retrospective observational study of factors associated with achieving adequate caloric delivery immediately after percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy. The feeding tube's early success factors were identified. The factors guide nutrition support.
pmc-13425543: In this 2026 gastric cancer paper, RUNX1-driven CPXM1 transcription promoted malignant phenotypes and EMT in gastric cancer cells. The transcription factor's target drove the cancer. The promoting is the mechanism.
pmc-13476643: A 2026 Chinese study (BASIC-OHCA registry) on emergency medical service organizational structure and prehospital outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (the title is truncated). The EMS organization affected survival. The insights inform system design.
pmc-13416743: A 2026 pharmacology paper measuring cerebrospinal fluid concentrations of bedaquiline, pretomanid, and linezolid during curative treatment of fluoroquinolone-resistant pre-extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (the title is truncated). The brain penetration was quantified. The concentrations guide TB meningitis care.
pmc-13420343: This 2026 case report described Hemoglobin Lepore-Boston-Washington — a rare cause of unmeasurable HbA1c and diagnostic challenge in diabetes. The variant hemoglobin fooled the test. The case warns laboratorians.
pmc-13418143: This 2026 paper showed forsythoside A alleviated experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis by targeting Tnfaip2. The plant compound calmed the MS model. The alleviating is the therapeutic mechanism.
pmc-13423143: A 2026 paper on extending the age limit of paediatric care for young people from refugee backgrounds. The care transition was examined. The extending is the equity question.
arxiv-2606-15943: A software engineering paper about how to model programs built around large language models. It combines graphs — pictures of connections between parts — with probability to describe how information flows through AI-powered software. The goal is to give engineers a clear, precise way to design and analyze systems where AI models generate much of the behavior.
arxiv-2606-16043: A stats paper that sharpens a go-to tool for linked yes-or-no data — say, did each twin quit smoking? The tool is called GEE, and the paper trims its slant with tuned math, plus a fix for odds-style readouts. It is for number pros who study grouped yes-or-no results.
arxiv-2606-16143: Random sampling is a workhorse of statistics and AI, and custom chips can run it far faster than general processors. AIA is a multi-core RISC-V processor built in 16-nanometer technology, customized for discrete sampling workloads. The paper describes the chip's design for engineers working on sampling-heavy computing.
arxiv-2606-16243: Transformers can memorize their training data instead of learning — overfitting. LiFT fights this with local search guided by linear programming, a classic optimization tool, to control overfitting during training. The paper presents the method for machine learning researchers who want more reliable transformer models.
arxiv-2606-16343: Type 2 active galactic nuclei are supermassive black holes hidden behind dust, and their light flickers over time. This astronomy paper studies that optical variability together with the motions of gas in their narrow-line regions. The combined view helps astronomers understand the hidden engines of these obscured galactic centers.
